text:
Cinema learned to talk today.

The Jazz Singer premiered in New York on 6 October 1927, 99 years ago.
It had about two minutes of synchronised talking. Al Jolson's first line: "Wait a minute, wait a minute, you ain't heard nothin' yet!"
Sam Warner, the Warner brother who pushed hardest for sound, died the day before the premiere.
India took four more years. Ardeshir Irani's Alam Ara opened at the Majestic Cinema, Bombay, on 14 March 1931.
Its "De De Khuda Ke Naam Pe" is counted as Hindi cinema's first song.
No print of Alam Ara survives. In 2017 the BFI called it the most important lost Indian film.
One lost film you'd bring back?
